clue.text: Endlessly frantic music ruins such examples of plainsong (11, two words)

indicators.note: ruins, as a verb, wrecks the letters of the remaining words so they are rebuilt in a new order
endlessly means the word frantic loses its final letter before use

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild music spoils the calm plainsong it is meant to accompany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims FRANTIC to FRANTI; 'ruins' rearranges FRANTI plus MUSIC into CANTUS FIRMI, the plural of cantus firmus.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantus firmus is a fixed melody, typically plainchant, around which other polyphonic voices are built.

clue.text: Cad's untruth is unveiled (about time) using swift and subtle argument

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the single letter for time
unveiled suggests the cad's untruth is exposed in a different form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the cad's supplies its letters including the S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bounder's lie is exposed at last, thanks to quick-witted debating.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the possessive S of the first word counts as a letter here; the bracketed phrase tells you a single time letter sits within the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and thrust is an idiom for lively, rapid exchange in debate, borrowed from swordplay.

clue.text: Bill admits 'I go ape, crazy', describing highest point

indicators.note: admits means the bill lets other letters in, so it goes round them

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: crazy says the words I go ape are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage on seeing the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'Bill' suggests a person, but it is an invoice, abbreviated as for account; Apogaeic is the rarer spelling of apogeic.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest or furthest point of an orbit, and this adjective is the form relating to it.

clue.text: Present batting indicating certain failure

parts.note: present, as in at this moment, means now
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator gloomily predicts the side now at the crease will lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is a defeat, so the phrase signals sure failure.

clue.text: Slap wife, getting thrown into US cell

indicators.note: getting thrown into places the wife's letter inside the cell

parts.note: tank is American slang for a prison cell

explanation.surface: A man who strikes his wife ends up in an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Twank is a dialect verb meaning to slap or smack sharply.

clue.text: Soup ingredient in tin? Mother'll treat growing bairn so

indicators.note: in places the soup ingredient within the chemical symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a pea is a typical ingredient of soup

explanation.surface: A Scottish mother serves tinned soup to her toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is a Scottish child; to spean is the Scots verb meaning to wean.
explanation.definitionFit: Spean is Scots for wean, what a mother does as a growing infant moves off breast milk.

clue.text: Pounce, maybe bent copper intercepting trap, amateur

indicators.note: intercepting means the copper gets in the way of, and so sits inside, the trap

parts.note: a fall, as in a deadfall, is a trap
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A crooked policeman catches someone with a trap, though he is no professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounce' is not a leap here but an old word for a bird of prey's claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcula is a sharply curved claw, and pounce is an old term for a hawk's talon.

clue.text: Grapevine yielding endless red wine

indicators.note: endless means the word red loses its last letter

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A vineyard turns out red wine from its grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grapevine' means the rumour mill, not a plant; 'endless' cuts RED to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the grapevine means rumour, and a report is likewise a piece of hearsay.

clue.text: Spoil child — you either love it or hate it!

definitions.text: you either love it or hate it!

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Spoiling a child is something people feel strongly about one way or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the long-running advertising slogan for a British yeast-extract spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeast spread famously advertised itself with a love-it-or-hate-it slogan.

clue.text: Reg and Ned drunk on binge — one appears to be batting for both sides!

definitions.text: one appears to be batting for both sides!

indicators.note: drunk says the letters of Reg and Ned are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a bender is a drinking binge

explanation.surface: Two men named Reg and Ned get drunk on a spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting for both sides' is slang for bisexual; here it hints at someone who blurs gender lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A gender bender dresses or behaves so as to blur the usual masculine and feminine roles.

clue.text: Ultra-modern step accepted by savant

indicators.note: accepted by means the step is taken inside the savant

parts.note: a sage is a learned person
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A scholar takes on board a forward move.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age is an adjective for something strikingly modern or futuristic.

clue.text: Plate used for weaving woollie I dispensed with

indicators.note: dispensed with means the letter I is dropped

parts.note: a cardi, short for cardigan, is a woolly garment

explanation.surface: A knitter gives up a cardigan for a weaving tool.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jacquard weaving a punched card is the plate that controls the pattern.

clue.text: Being drawn in the direction of battle

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
wage, as in wage war, means to fight or carry on a battle

explanation.surface: Troops are heading off towards a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Towage is the act of hauling something along by a tow rope.

clue.text: Border, one surrounding tart

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for one goes round the tart

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
pro, short for prostitute, is slang for a tart

explanation.surface: A single person loiters at the edge round a woman of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a fringe or border, such as the stage apron or the grass round a putting green.

clue.text: Man regarded as usual to trap king

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A man is seen as setting a trap for a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Gink is slang for a fellow, a chap who is nothing out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Cash discount covers capital drawn by e.g. crook

indicators.note: covers means the abbreviation goes round the capital

parts.note: CD is the abbreviation for cash discount
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A bargain price conceals a crooked deal in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A crome is a dialect word for a hooked stick or crook; cromed means dragged with one.
explanation.definitionFit: To crome is to drag with a hooked tool, so something cromed has been hauled by such a crook.

clue.text: Granny appears before the family in browny yellow cotton

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
kin means one's family

explanation.surface: Grandma turns up ahead of the relatives dressed in khaki-ish cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankin, or nankeen, is a buff-yellow cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Pieces Leopold Mozart initially composed without frills

indicators.note: composed, as of music, means these letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of Leopold and Mozart

explanation.surface: Mozart's father wrote some plain, unadorned pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Semplice is a musical direction meaning simply, apt for the composer surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Semplice instructs a performer to play simply, without ornament.

clue.text: Shortfall ICI disposed of — that's handy

indicators.note: disposed of means the letters of ICI are removed

parts.note: a deficit is a shortfall

explanation.surface: A chemicals firm gets rid of its losses, which is useful.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a large British chemicals company.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft and handy both describe someone skilful and nimble with their hands.

clue.text: Tip for reinforcing regulation: one doing so must come up on top

indicators.note: on top places the reversed piece above the other in the down entry
in a down answer coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is one who enforces regulation
a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: Advice on enforcing rules: the enforcer must rise to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one doing so' refers back to regulating: a REF, which 'must come up' turns to FER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferrule is a metal cap or ring that strengthens the end of a stick or handle.

clue.text: Second leader of pack with cubs? A real headache

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of pack

parts.note: a litter is a brood of cubs

explanation.surface: A wolf pack's deputy leader with young cubs finds them a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A splitter is an informal word for a splitting headache, a very painful one.

clue.text: Volcanic glass for each illuminated tip of torchère

parts.note: per means for each
lit means illuminated

indicators.note: tip of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Each lamp stand is lit at its top.
explanation.walkthrough: A torchère is a tall ornamental stand for a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Perlite is a glassy volcanic rock that expands when heated.

clue.text: Bier fashioned in wood — means of precluding overlong struggle?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters of bier are shaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coffin stand made of hardwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bier' and 'wood' together suggest a coffin, but the definition is from tennis, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak decides a tennis set level on games, stopping it going on indefinitely.

clue.text: 'Don't let your spirits fail' — attention in boozer raised (6, two words)

indicators.note: in places the attention inside the raised pub
raised, in a down entry, means the word for boozer reads upwards

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub
ear means attention, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to cheer up while listening in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear up is an idiom meaning keep going cheerfully despite hardship.

clue.text: Last bits of steak available form lamb curry?

indicators.note: last bits of takes the final letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A diner asks if there is lamb curry, with the steak sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' is the verb meaning to groom a horse; kemb is an old word for comb.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemb is an archaic form of comb, and to curry is to comb a horse's coat.

clue.text: 'Totty', name accepted by girl informally

indicators.note: accepted by means the name's letter is taken inside the girl

parts.note: bit, as in bit of fluff, is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is happy to be called Totty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bint and totty are both British slang, often derogatory, for a woman or young woman.

clue.text: Grade exercises 'plain'

parts.note: a step is a grade or degree
PE, physical education, means exercises

explanation.surface: Graded exercises are described as simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassy plain, as in Russia or Central Asia.

clue.text: Malefic ——, I'll bedevil Islamic belief

indicators.note: bedevil means the blank plus malefic and I are jumbled together to form the closing phrase

parts.note: taken as written
I'll contributes the single letter I

explanation.surface: A wicked demon vows to torment Muslim faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite: the answer plus MALEFIC and I, mixed together ('bedevil'), spell ISLAMIC BELIEF; the blank is the answer's place in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eblis is a name for the devil in Islamic tradition, so malevolence and Islamic belief both fit.

clue.text: Pet to cage up on end of leash

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the word for cage reads upwards

parts.note: a coop is a cage for poultry

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of leash

explanation.surface: Instructions to shut a pet in its cage once off the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is informal for a dog, the typical household pet.

clue.text: Set back after crash perhaps, a long time before I'll enter core of sterling

indicators.note: enter means the preceding letters go inside the core
core of takes the middle letters of sterling

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
I'll, read as I will, supplies I, with will forming part of the instruction

explanation.surface: A long while passes before I'll get to the heart of the pound's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: The I comes from 'I'll' read as 'I will', so the 'will' simply joins the instruction to enter; the core of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerail is to set a derailed train back on the track, as after a crash.

clue.text: 'Omeless fellow left little money in ancient times

parts.note: a homeless fellow is a hobo, and the dropped H of the Cockney spelling drops the H here too

explanation.surface: A Cockney tramp left a coin long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: E.g. Wellington's vengeance leading navy in volte-face

indicators.note: leading places the vengeance before the navy

parts.note: utu is the Maori word for vengeance, used in New Zealand, whose capital is Wellington
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington takes revenge at the head of the fleet with a sudden change of course.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington is the New Zealand capital, not the duke; UTU is the New Zealand word for revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn and a volte-face both mean a complete reversal of direction or policy.

clue.text: Rough scar tissue, nothing like properly treated, departs ultimately

indicators.note: properly treated means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs, here placed at the end

explanation.surface: A scar that looks nothing like one which has been properly dressed eventually fades.
explanation.definitionFit: A keloid is a raised, irregular overgrowth of fibrous tissue at a scar.

clue.text: Behave like a bad pen with no issue left to publish?

parts.note: SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in family trees
to utter is to put into circulation or make public

explanation.surface: A childless author leaves something to be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no issue' refers to having no children, not to a magazine issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty pen splutters, spitting ink irregularly as it writes.

clue.text: Corded cloth, soft on the lady's charger

parts.note: rep is a fabric with a corded surface
lenis is the phonetic term for a soft consonant
her means belonging to the lady

explanation.surface: A ribbed fabric, gentle on a woman's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' is not a horse but something that fills or charges, such as a battery charger.
explanation.definitionFit: A replenisher refills or recharges, and in electrics is a device that maintains a charge.
